stories.body: Kuwait said Wednesday it was countering hostile drones, while Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian attacks, as Gulf states remained on alert following an American strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island. Tehran said it had targeted a US base in Kuwait; Bahrain condemned the attacks. The exchanges come amid a continuing standoff over the Strait of Hormuz. The supplied reports do not establish the extent of damage or casualties.
stories.headline: Kuwait and Bahrain report fresh attacks after US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island

stories.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday. Xi began bilateral talks with Vladimir Putin ahead of an expected meeting involving the Chinese, Russian and US leaders on Thursday. Trade tensions and new American restrictions on chip exports are expected to feature prominently. The gathering gives Xi an opportunity to present China as a diplomatic power broker while Putin and Donald Trump face wars they have struggled to end.
stories.headline: Xi opens APEC with calls for AI cooperation ahead of talks with Putin and Trump

stories.body: Ukrainian attacks on Monday and Tuesday caused structural damage to the Kerch bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea, closing the road crossing while rail services reportedly resumed after several hours. Published images showed a collapsed arch and a section of roadway in the water. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the operation had been prepared over several weeks and used Ukrainian drones and missiles. Participants described waves of drones intended to overwhelm Russian air defences, with additional drones relaying radio signals. Moscow acknowledged damage and promised repairs. The attack disrupts an important Russian military supply route and damages a symbol of Putin’s rule ahead of his meetings in China.
stories.headline: Ukraine damages Kerch bridge ahead of Putin’s summit with Xi and Trump

stories.body: Israel’s parliament elected Matan Kahana as speaker by 66 votes to 52, giving opponents of Benjamin Netanyahu control over the legislative timetable while coalition negotiations continue. Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, won with support from Jewish-led opposition parties and Arab-led parties. Eisenkot is trying to form a government following the October 27 election, in which neither his bloc nor Netanyahu’s secured a majority. His allies want to reverse measures weakening judicial independence, introduce prime ministerial term limits and establish a state inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attacks. The speakership could help them advance those bills, although parliamentary procedures and the limited coalition-building window remain obstacles.
stories.headline: Netanyahu’s opponents elect Matan Kahana as Israeli parliament speaker

stories.body: Police raided Sozcu TV’s Istanbul headquarters on Tuesday as Turkish authorities took over the pro-opposition broadcaster. France 24 described it as the third seizure of an opposition media outlet in just over a year. The move comes amid public anger over an investment fund scandal involving billions and affecting the savings of nearly half a million people, adding pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling AKP ahead of elections in 2028.
stories.headline: Turkish authorities seize opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

stories.body: Public sector workers held their third united day of strikes and demonstrations since September on Tuesday, demanding broad pay rises and stronger public services after talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu failed to satisfy unions. The interior ministry counted 146,000 demonstrators nationwide, down from 575,000 at the previous unified protests; unions put Tuesday’s turnout at 550,000. France’s 5.8 million public sector employees had been urged to mobilise over living costs and squeezed services, following a minimum wage increase for private-sector workers the previous week.
stories.headline: French public sector workers strike for higher pay as turnout falls

stories.body: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, according to the Associated Press call reported Tuesday night, completing a nine-seat Democratic gain and a 56–44 Senate majority. The former representative will become the first Alaska Native senator after campaigning on high costs and an Alaska-first platform. The result could face legal challenges: the Justice Department sued to block certification if Sullivan lost, citing confusion involving another candidate named Dan Sullivan. Peltola denied knowledge of an alleged effort by campaign aides to recruit the namesake candidate. Alaska also elected Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins as governor.
stories.headline: Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race, giving Democrats a 56-seat majority

stories.body: Nvidia’s board said it would not reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang following his resignation over conduct the company said breached its standards. Interim CEO Colette Kress is leading the company while directors seek a permanent replacement. Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecast $130 billion for the next quarter. Huang has agreed to testify before congressional committees on December 1 amid allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence asset and scrutiny of chip sales through Singapore-based Megaspeed. US authorities have confirmed a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, while tighter export rules could affect Nvidia’s business.
stories.headline: Nvidia rules out Huang’s return as revenue doubles and congressional scrutiny grows

stories.body: International health officials said Tuesday that the United States, Mexico and Bolivia had lost their measles-elimination status as transmission continued across the Americas. France 24 reported that the virus was spreading in the US at its fastest rate in more than 30 years. Falling vaccination rates in the US and elsewhere have accompanied the resurgence, with measles spreading across the region since 2024. The loss of elimination status marks a reversal of a major public health achievement.
stories.headline: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-elimination status

stories.body: The FAA oversaw and approved repair work preceding a nationwide ground stop, according to The Washington Post. A person familiar with the investigation said public blame directed at contractor L3Harris overlooked the agency’s involvement. A separate report examined Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s proposed $50 billion funding package, finding that only part would go toward air traffic modernisation and reporting experts’ doubts that funding alone would prevent another shutdown.
stories.headline: FAA’s role in repairs before nationwide ground stop comes under scrutiny

stories.body: The government approved an increase in the minimum wage to €1,286 gross per month in 14 payments from January, equivalent to €18,004 annually and €65 more per payment. The 5.3% rise exceeds both inflation through October and the advisory commission’s 4.9% recommendation, but falls short of unions’ 7% demand. Tax changes are intended to keep minimum wage earners free of income tax without monthly withholding; those measures still require parliamentary approval. Ministers also approved a 4.5% public sector pay rise, subject to ratification. Business groups criticised the process, with Catalan employers’ association Pimec warning that higher labour costs could constrain smaller firms.
stories.headline: Spain approves 5.3% minimum wage increase and 4.5% public sector pay rise for 2027

stories.body: Spanish police have asked the judge investigating July’s mass irregular crossings into Ceuta to seek information from Google and Meta about 97 connections involving phone numbers that may belong to Moroccan security or intelligence personnel. Investigators traced contacts linked to administrators and organisers of WhatsApp groups, using third-party address books and leaked records to identify possible connections. The findings challenge the CNI intelligence service’s assessment discounting Moroccan responsibility, but police acknowledge that the fragmented organisation makes it difficult to establish who directed the crossings. The requested checks are intended to confirm identities and strengthen the evidence; the reported connections do not establish state orchestration.
stories.headline: Police seek checks on possible Moroccan security links to Ceuta crossing networks

stories.body: Government lawyers told the Supreme Court that 113,326 naturalised Spaniards will be unable to vote in the November 29 general election because of its suspension affecting people granted citizenship under the Democratic Memory Law, commonly called the grandchildren law. The suspension excludes those with certificates establishing that they are children or grandchildren of political exiles. The government reduced its initial estimate of 163,020 affected people after removing minors and those absent from the August 1 electoral register used for this election.
stories.headline: Government puts number barred from voting under nationality ruling at 113,326

stories.body: The Generalitat opened an inquiry into Renfe over last week’s Rodalies disruption, including failures to provide minimum services during strikes on November 10 and 11 and up to 1,600 cancellations counted by passenger groups. A further inquiry could follow Tuesday’s strike, when 41% of designated minimum services did not run. Drivers’ union Semaf said staff had not been properly notified, while Renfe and the government maintained that notifications had been issued. La Vanguardia highlighted the dispute over sending notices by email outside working hours. The inquiry could lead to financial penalties for Renfe. Rodalies also warned of possible disruption Wednesday morning because some trains had not reached their starting stations.
stories.headline: Generalitat investigates Renfe as rail strike again falls short of minimum services

stories.body: A security breach at website personalisation provider Optimizely allowed attackers to inject malicious JavaScript into customer websites, with 178 companies reportedly affected, including Ikea, Zoom, Salesforce, the BBC and CNN. According to 3Cat, the code operated for about 16 hours and could capture information entered into legitimate forms, including payment card details, as well as accessible cookies and screenshots. It also reportedly replaced cryptocurrency wallet addresses, diverting about $7,043. Optimizely said early Tuesday that it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the code and contacted affected organisations. The attack exploited a shared supplier rather than requiring separate intrusions into each company’s servers.
stories.headline: Optimizely breach exposes visitors to malicious code on major websites

stories.body: The Generalitat ordered public land agency Incasòl to sell more than 132,000 square metres at the El Molló industrial estate for the proposed AI gigafactory in Móra la Nova. The project envisages up to €5 billion in investment, mostly from European funds, but still depends on an EU selection process whose application deadline has moved to December 3, with a decision expected early next year. Spain has approved €719 million in public investment, while the consortium includes Telefónica, Santander, ACS and Multiverse Computing. Opposition groups warn about energy demand and local impacts; roughly 3,000 people joined a broader rural protest in Móra d’Ebre over the weekend.
stories.headline: Catalan government approves land sale for proposed Móra la Nova AI gigafactory

stories.body: Teaching and student unions, family federation aFFaC and other education organisations have called a demonstration at Plaça d’Urquinaona at noon on Saturday, November 21. Their joint manifesto calls for public education that is inclusive, democratic and taught in Catalan, with education spending reaching at least 6% of GDP. They want smaller classes, stronger support for pupils with additional needs, better staff pay and stability, and public funding for meals, transport, materials and school activities. Organisers also urge the government to use falling pupil numbers to reduce class sizes rather than close public school classes or centres, and to progressively reduce public subsidies to privately run schools.
stories.headline: Teachers, students and families call Barcelona march for public education on Saturday
